subject.title: fix(agents): guard CLI MCP resume reuse

question: Should stored CLI bindings with a strict `mcpResumeHash` be reset whenever the current run cannot reproduce that strict topology proof, rather than falling back to a matching raw `mcpConfigHash`?
rationale: The patch is mechanically narrow and source-correct, but it deliberately changes upgrade behavior for persisted CLI sessions and therefore needs an explicit owner decision on the fail-closed compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Accept strict topology invalidation
options.body: Rebase and merge the guard, accepting a one-time reset for affected stored CLI sessions when strict MCP resume proof is unavailable.

options.title: Keep raw-config fallback
options.body: Decline the guard and preserve existing session reuse when the raw MCP configuration still matches despite missing resume-hash proof.

options.title: Decide with broader lifecycle work
options.body: Pause this narrow PR until the broader CLI binding lifecycle policy in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/84593 is decided.

recommendation.title: Accept strict topology invalidation
recommendation.body: Rebase and merge the guard, accepting a one-time reset for affected stored CLI sessions when strict MCP resume proof is unavailable.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the strict MCP resume-hash invariant and are best placed to decide whether missing current proof should invalidate existing bindings.
